text.p: The following are the leading stories in the Maltese press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Leader of the opposition Fenech Adami tells Prime Minister Sant to come clean on austerity. He says the prime minister should declare his government intends belt-tightening if that is the case. The new Labour government has complained that it found the country's financial situation in a mess.
- Car thieves become more discriminating, go for high-value cars.
- Equivalent of $2.8 million earmarked for exhibition site.
- Government studies better use of valleys. Agriculture Minister Michael Farrugia said precious natural water was being lost because valleys were not looked after.

- Malta humiliated in Dublin. Opposition leader Fenech Adami attacks the government for not having been represented at the Dublin EU summit. Malta, he said, had been at the top of the EU list of potential new members. Now it was at the bottom. The new Labour government has declared that Malta's six-year-old EU application is "frozen" while Malta and the EU explore a new framework for mutually beneficial relations.
